serious.title: CORE-COMP-008 fails at the board-size cap: compile returns a command that apply refuses with core/cap on the same view
serious.clause: CORE-COMP-008; §13.3 G6 ('every check apply would make ... caps'); brief point 3. The MUST is broken, which by common.md's first rule is high. I rated it medium because it needs a board of about 59 MiB, which is outside ordinary use, and because §16 has no compile code for it. The lead should settle the severity.

fixed: CORE-COMP-008 at the board-size cap: the reproduction is now in crates/taskdeck-core/tests/probe_verify.rs. On 814b88c it failed with Err("core/cap") vs Ok(()). Cause: compile never ran apply's size check (§8.4 step 4, CORE-APPLY-005). Fix: src/apply.rs gains pub(crate) `refused_for_size(board, command, ctx)`. It uses apply's own bounds (`size_bound`, `growth_bound`, `canonical_len`) and, only near the cap, runs the effects on a clone. It returns true only when the checks pass and the effects leave bytes over 61,865,984 and longer than before. src/compile.rs `compile` now calls it on `view` after the G8 check, before storing the minter back, so on refusal the minter is unchanged (CORE-COMP-004). The Ctx it uses has seq = 2^53-1 (the longest stamps, so a command that fits under it fits under any seq), device_no = origin, at = now and based_on = seq-1. A refusal is `core/cap`, 400, "The board is full." (SPEC-QUESTION in place). This covers every growing command: creates, add_block, rename, set_notes and the others. A second test checks that a shrinking command (delete) at the cap still compiles and applies.
for_lead: §16 has no compile code for a command apply would refuse for size (§8.4 step 4), but G6 and CORE-COMP-008 require compile to refuse it on `view`. Reading 1: add a §16 row for it (code, status, message). Reading 2: leave compile silent, which contradicts CORE-COMP-008. Taken: apply's `core/cap`, status 400, message "The board is full." (after §16's 'the UI says the board is full'). It is marked SPEC-QUESTION in src/compile.rs. The spec should settle the row and the exact text.
Severity of the finding (the checker rated it medium, and by common.md's first rule a broken MUST is high): the lead should settle it.
